name: llm-eval-builder
description: Use when designing or building evaluations for LLM apps: golden datasets, LLM-as-judge rubrics, regression suites, CI eval jobs, or comparing prompt or model variants on an eval set. Not for automatically improving the system under test.

name: prompt-writing
description: Use when drafting, rewriting, or critiquing a prompt or system prompt by hand: structure, role, examples, output format, and common failure modes. Produces a single improved prompt with an explanation.

name: performance-profiling
description: Use when code is slow or uses too much memory: profile first (py-spy, perf, Instruments, cProfile), find the hot path, then apply targeted fixes such as better data structures, batching, caching, or removing N+1 queries.

name: web-performance
description: Use when a web frontend is slow to load or interact: bundle size, code splitting, tree-shaking, lazy loading, image optimization, Core Web Vitals, and Lighthouse audits.

name: code-review
description: Use when reviewing a diff, PR, or file for correctness bugs, security issues, readability, and maintainability. Returns prioritized findings with suggested fixes.

name: hyperparameter-tuning
description: Use when tuning numeric hyperparameters of ML models (learning rate, depth, regularization) with Optuna, Ray Tune, or grid/random/Bayesian search, including search spaces, pruning, and cross-validation.

name: llm-finetuning
description: Use when training or fine-tuning model weights: SFT, LoRA/QLoRA, DPO, dataset formatting, training configs, and evaluating checkpoints.

name: sql-expert
description: Use when writing, debugging, or speeding up SQL queries: EXPLAIN plans, indexes, joins, window functions, query rewrites, and schema design for Postgres, MySQL, and SQLite.

name: systematic-debugging
description: Use when encountering a bug, test failure, crash, or unexpected behavior: reproduce, form hypotheses, bisect, read logs and traces, and confirm the root cause before proposing a fix.

name: writing-editor
description: Use when editing prose: tightening paragraphs, fixing tone and grammar, improving resumes, cover letters, emails, blog posts, and docs for clarity and concision.

name: planning
description: Use when the user wants a plan: breaking down a project, roadmap, career or life plan, or multi-step implementation into milestones, dependencies, and next actions.

name: test-driven-development
description: Use when implementing a feature or bugfix: write failing tests first (unit, property, edge cases), then the minimal code to pass, then refactor.

name: dataviz
description: Use when creating any chart, plot, or dashboard: choosing the chart form, color palette, axes, legends, and annotations in matplotlib, plotly, d3, or Recharts.

name: deep-research
description: Use when a question needs research across multiple sources (papers, docs, blogs) and a synthesized, cited answer: comparing methods, explaining a technique, or surveying a field.
